readings.subtitle: The Explanation for All Things
readings.text: [John 1:1] In the beginning was <dn><kw1>the Word</kw1></dn>, and <dn><kw1>the Word</kw1></dn> was <kw45>with</kw45> <dn><kw2>Elohim</kw2></dn>, and <dn><kw1>the Word</kw1></dn> was <dn><kw2>Elohim</kw2></dn>. <vid:sUOJMopNKrI?start=398>

readings.title: A Unified Cycle
readings.subtitle: The Generation of Illumination
readings.text: [Genesis 1:1] <h7225>In the beginning</h7225> <dn>Elohim</dn> <kw33>created</kw33> <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> the earth. {1.1} <vid:tlXLHUIDl1Y?start=1> [2] Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was on the face of the deep. <img:Waters 1.jpg, Waters 2.jpg, Waters 3.jpg, Waters 4.jpg, Waters 5.jpg, Waters 6.jpg, Waters 7.jpg> And the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> was <kw3>moving</kw3> on the face of the waters. <img:Spirit 1.jpg, Spirit 2.jpg, Spirit 3.jpg> <vid:mg96tfzD-eE?start=1> [3] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Let <kw4>light</kw4> come to be,”</dq> and <kw4>light</kw4> came to be. [4] And <dn>Elohim</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> the <kw4>light</kw4>, that it was <kw5>good</kw5>. And <dn>Elohim</dn> separated the <kw4>light</kw4> from the darkness. <vid:lJS7YqccVAM?start=1> [5] And <dn>Elohim</dn> called the <kw4>light</kw4> <dq>‘a <kw6>day</kw6>’</dq> and the darkness <dn>He</dn> called <dq>‘a night.’</dq> And there came to be evening and there came to be morning, <kw7>one day</kw7>.{5.1}

footnotes.1.1:
The Nature of Elohim

The term Elohim here is the plural of Eloah, yet it is used with the singular verb Bara (created). This grammatical construct signifies:

  • The Unity: One singular entity acting.
  • The Majesty: Plural form denotes supreme authority and fullness.
  • The Complexity: Hints at the multi-faceted nature of the Creator.

HebrewTypeMeaning
ElohimPluralSupreme Power
EloahSingularGod / Deity
“The mystery of the Creator is hidden in the grammar of His name.” – Ancient Commentary

readings.title: A Second Cycle
readings.subtitle: The Expansion of the Heavens
readings.text: [Genesis 1:6] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let it separate the waters from the waters.”</dq> [7] And <dn>Elohim</dn> made <dn>את</dn> the expanse, and separated the waters which were under the expanse from the waters which were above the expanse. And it came to be so. [8] And <dn>Elohim</dn> called the expanse <dq>‘heavens.’</dq> And there came to be evening and there came to be morning, the second <kw6>day</kw6>.

readings.text: [Genesis 1:9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together into <kw8>one place</kw8>, and let the dry land appear.”</dq> And it came to be so. [10] And <dn>Elohim</dn> called the dry land <dq>‘earth,’</dq> and the gathering together of the waters <dn>He</dn> called <dq>‘seas.’</dq> And <dn>Elohim</dn> saw that it was <kw5>good</kw5>. <vid:B9vEdhrcMyw?start=1> [11] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb that yields seed, and the fruit tree that yields fruit according to its kind, whose seed is in itself, on the earth.”</dq> And it came to be so. [12] And the earth brought forth grass, the herb that yields seed according to its kind, and the tree that yields fruit, whose seed is in itself according to its kind. And <dn>Elohim</dn> saw that it was <kw5>good</kw5>. [13] And there came to be evening and there came to be morning, the third <kw6>day</kw6>. <vid:ovJwgkcPAiw?start=1>

readings.text: [Genesis 1:14] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Let lights come to be in the expanse of the heavens to separate the day from the night, and let them be for signs and appointed times, and for days <img:days.PNG> and years <img:years.PNG>,</dq> [15] <dq>and let them be for lights in the expanse of the heavens to give <kw4>light</kw4> on the earth.”</dq> And it came to be so. [16] And <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>את</dn> made two great lights: <dn>את</dn> the greater <kw4>light</kw4> to rule the day, and <dn>את</dn> the lesser <kw4>light</kw4> to rule the night <img:lesser_light.PNG,yeshua_geneology.PNG>, and <dn>את</dn> the stars. [17] And <dn>Elohim</dn> set <dn>את</dn> them in the expanse of the heavens to give <kw4>light</kw4> on the earth, [18] and to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate the <kw4>light</kw4> from the darkness. And <dn>Elohim</dn> saw that it was <kw5>good</kw5>. [19] And there came to be evening and there came to be morning, the fourth <kw6>day</kw6>. <vid:qe-AkwpzzIs?start=1>

readings.title: A Fifth Cycle
readings.subtitle: Life and Blessing
readings.text: [Genesis 1:20] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Let the waters teem with shoals of living beings, and let birds fly above the earth on the face of the expanse of the heavens.”</dq> [21] And <dn>Elohim</dn> <kw33>created</kw33> <dn>את</dn> <kw34>great sea creatures</kw34> and <dn>את</dn> every living being that moves with which the waters teemed, according to their kind, and <dn>את</dn> every winged bird according to its kind. And <dn>Elohim</dn> saw that it was <kw5>good</kw5>. [22] And <dn>Elohim</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> them, saying, <dq>“Be fruitful and increase, and fill <dn>את</dn> the waters in the seas, and let the birds increase on the earth.”</dq> [23] And there came to be evening and there came to be morning, the fifth <kw6>day</kw6>.

readings.title: The Sixth Cycle
readings.subtitle: The Work is Finished with the Crowning Glory
readings.text: [Genesis 1:24] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Let the earth bring forth the living being according to its kind: livestock and creeping creatures and beasts of the earth, according to its kind.”</dq> And it came to be so. [25] And <dn>Elohim</dn> made <dn>את</dn> the living ones of the earth according to its kind, <dn>את</dn> livestock according to its kind, and <dn>את</dn> all that creep on the earth according to its kind. And <dn>Elohim</dn> saw that it was <kw5>good</kw5>. [26] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“Let us make a <kw36>man</kw36> in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the heavens, and over the livestock, and over all the earth and over all the creeping creatures that creep on the ground.”</dq> [27] And <dn>Elohim</dn> <kw33>created</kw33> <dn>את</dn> the <kw36>man</kw36> in His image, in the image of <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>He</dn> <kw33>created</kw33> <dn>את</dn> him – male and female He <kw33>created</kw33> <dn>את</dn> them. [28] And <dn>Elohim</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> them, and <dn>Elohim</dn> said to them, <dq>“Be fruitful and increase, and fill <dn>את</dn> the earth and subdue it, and rule over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the heavens, and over all creeping creatures on the earth.”</dq> [29] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“See, I have given you <dn>את</dn> every plant that yields seed which is on the face of all the earth, and <dn>את</dn> every tree whose fruit yields seed, to you it is for food.</dq> [30] <dq>And to every beast of the earth, and to every bird of the heavens, and to every creeping creature on the earth, in which there is a living being, <dn>את</dn> every green plant is for food.”</dq> And it came to be so. [31] And <dn>Elohim</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>He</dn> had made, and see, it was <kw9>very good</kw9>. And there came to be evening and there came to be morning, the sixth <kw6>day</kw6>.

[2] And in the seventh <kw6>day</kw6> <dn>Elohim</dn> completed <dn>His</dn> work which <dn>He</dn> had done, and <dn>He</dn> <kw35>rested</kw35> on the seventh <kw6>day</kw6> from all His work which <dn>He</dn> had made. [3] And <dn>Elohim</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> the seventh <kw6>day</kw6> and <kw11>set</kw11> <dn>את</dn> it <kw12>apart</kw12>, because on it <dn>He</dn> <kw35>rested</kw35> from all His work which <dn>Elohim</dn> <kw38>in creating had made</kw38>. <img:shavua.PNG> [4] These are the births of the heavens and the earth when they were <kw33>created</kw33>, in the <kw6>day</kw6> {4.1} that <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> made earth and heavens. <vid:hdvYdhd4vvs?start=1>

readings.title: Creation Recap
readings.text: [Genesis 2:5] Now no shrub of the field was yet on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprung up, for <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> had not sent rain on the earth, and there was no <kw36>man</kw36> to till the <dn>את</dn> ground, [6] but a mist went up from the earth and watered <dn>את</dn> the entire surface of the ground. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> formed <dn>את</dn> the <kw36>man</kw36> out of dust from the ground, and breathed into his nostrils <kw14>breath of lives</kw14>. And the <kw36>man</kw36> became a living being. [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> planted a garden in Ěḏen, to the east, and there He put <dn>את</dn> the <kw36>man</kw36> whom He had formed. [9] And out of the ground <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> made every tree grow that is pleasant to the sight and <kw5>good</kw5> for food, with <kw15>the tree of life</kw15> in the midst of the garden and <kw16>the tree of the knowledge of good and evil</kw16>. [10] Now a river went out from Ěḏen to water <dn>את</dn> the garden, and from there it divided and became four heads. [11] The name of the first is Pishon, it is the one surrounding <dn>את</dn> the entire land of Ḥavilah, where there is gold. [12] And the gold of that land is <kw5>good</kw5> Bdellium is there, and the shoham stone. [13] And the name of the second river is Giḥon, it is the one surrounding <dn>את</dn> the entire land of Kush. [14] And the name of the third river is Ḥiddeqel, it is the one which goes toward the east of Ashshur. And the fourth river is the pherat. [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> took <dn>את</dn> the <kw36>man</kw36> and put him in the garden of Ěḏen to work it and to guard it. [16] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> commanded the <kw36>man</kw36>, saying, <dq>“<kw17>Eat</kw17> of every tree of the garden,</dq> [17] <dq>but do not eat of <kw16>the tree of the knowledge of good and evil</kw16>, for in the <kw6>day</kw6> that you eat of it <kw18>you shall certainly die</kw18>.”</dq> [18] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“It is not <kw5>good</kw5> for the <kw36>man</kw36> to be alone, I am going to make <kw13>a helper for him, as his counterpart</kw13>.”</dq> {18.1} [19] And from the ground <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> formed <dn>את</dn> every beast of the field and <dn>את</dn> every bird of the heavens, and brought them to the <kw36>man</kw36> to see what he would call them. And whatever the <kw36>man</kw36> called each living being, that was its name. [20] So the <kw36>man</kw36> gave names to all livestock, and to the birds of the heavens, and to every beast of the field. But for the <kw36>man</kw36> there was not found <kw13>a helper for him, as his counterpart</kw13>. [21] So <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> caused a deep sleep to fall on the <kw36>man</kw36>, and he slept. And He took one of his <kw19>ribs</kw19> {21.1}, and closed up the flesh in its place. [22] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> made <dn>את</dn> the <kw20>rib</kw20> which He had taken from the <kw36>man</kw36> into a woman, and He brought her to the <kw36>man</kw36>. [23] And the <kw36>man</kw36> said, “Now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. This one is called ‘woman,’ because she was taken out of a man.” [24] For this cause shall a man leave <dn>את</dn> his father and <dn>את</dn> his mother, and cleave to his <kw29>wife</kw29>, and they shall become <kw23>one flesh</kw23>. [25] And they were both naked, the <kw36>man</kw36> and his <kw29>wife</kw29>, and they were not ashamed.

footnotes.18.1:
The Nature of the Ally (Ezer)

The Hebrew term Ezer describes a vital function rather than a specific rank. It refers to one who provides essential aid, defense, or support that the receiver cannot provide for themselves. While often translated as "helper," the term "Ally" better captures the military and vital context of the word without forcing a hierarchy.

  • The Meaning: The Paleo-Hebrew roots (Eye + Weapon) depict one who sees a need and acts to defend or supply it.
  • The Spectrum of Strength: The word is status-agnostic. It is used of God (Superior Aid), political alliances (Equal Aid), and here of the woman. It does not dictate that the parties are equal in strength, only that the aid is indispensable.
  • The Conclusion: An ally may provide 90% of the strength or 10%; the definition holds true as long as their contribution is necessary for the mission's success.

TranslationImplied RankTheological Fit
HelperFixed SubordinateLimited: Does not fit when God is the Helper.
AllyVariable (Sup/Eq/Inf)Accurate: Fits God, nations, and woman interchangeably.
“The Ezer is the one who supplies the lack. Whether superior or subordinate, the Ally is the essential component that moves the situation from 'not good' to 'very good'.”

readings.title: The Deception
readings.text: [Genesis 3:1] And the naḥash was more crafty than all the lives of the field which <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> had made, and he said to the woman, “Is it true that <dn>Elohim</dn> has said, ‘Do not eat of every tree of the garden’?” [2] And the woman said to the naḥash, “We are to eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden, [3] but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, <dn>Elohim</dn> has said, ‘Do not eat of it, nor touch it, lest you die.’ ” [4] And the naḥash said to the woman, “Not dying you will die. [5] “For knows <dn>Elohim</dn> that in the <kw6>day</kw6> you eat of it your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be like <dn>Elohim</dn>, <kw24>knowing good and evil</kw24>.” [6] And the woman saw that the tree was <kw5>good</kw5> for food, that it was pleasant to the eyes, and the tree desirable to make one wise, and she took of its fruit and ate. And she also gave to her <kw25>husband</kw25> with her, and he ate. [7] Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig leaves together and made <kw26>loin coverings</kw26> for themselves. [8] And they heard <dn>את the voice of YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> walking about in the garden in the cool of the day, and the <kw36>man</kw36> and his <kw29>wife</kw29> hid themselves from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> among the trees of the garden. [9] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> called unto the <kw36>man</kw36> and said to him, <dq>“Where are you?”</dq> [10] And he said, “I heard <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your voice</dn> in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid myself.” [11] And He said, <dq>“Who made you know that you were naked? Have you eaten of the tree of which I commanded you that you should not eat?”</dq> [12] And the <kw36>man</kw36> said, “The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me of the tree and I ate.” [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> said to the woman, <dq>“What is this you have done?”</dq> And the woman said, “The naḥash deceived me, and I ate.” [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> said to the naḥash, <dq>“Because you have done this, you are <kw32>cursed</kw32> more than all livestock and more than <kw27>every beast</kw27> of the field. On your belly you are to go, and eat dust all the days of your life.</dq> [15] <dq>And I put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and <dn>her Seed</dn>. <dn>He</dn> shall crush your head, and you shall crush <dn>His</dn> heel.”</dq> [16] To the woman <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> greatly increase your sorrow and your conception – bring forth children in pain. And your desire is for your <kw25>husband</kw25>, and he does rule over you.”</dq> [17] And to <kw28>the man</kw28> <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Because you have listened to the voice of your <kw29>wife</kw29>, and have eaten of the tree of which I commanded you, saying, ‘Do not eat of it’: “<kw32>cursed</kw32> is the ground because of you, in toil you are to eat of it all the days of your life,</dq> [18] <dq>and the ground shall bring forth thorns and thistles for you, and you shall eat <dn>את</dn> the herb of the field.</dq> [19] <dq>By the sweat of your face you are to eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken. For dust you are, and to dust you return.</dq> [20] And the <kw36>man</kw36> called his <kw29>wife</kw29>’s name Ḥavvah, because she became the mother of all living. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> made coats of skin for the <kw36>man</kw36> and his <kw29>wife</kw29> and dressed them. [22] And <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“See, the <kw36>man</kw36> has become like one of us, to <kw31>know good and evil</kw31>. And now, lest he put out his hand and take also of <kw15>the tree of life</kw15>, and eat, and live forever...”</dq> [23] so <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> sent him out of the garden of Ěḏen to till <dn>את</dn> the ground from which he was taken, [24] and <dn>He</dn> drove out <dn>את</dn> the <kw36>man</kw36>. And <dn>He</dn> placed <dn>את</dn> <kw30>keruḇim</kw30> at the east of the garden of Ěḏen, and <dn>את</dn> <kw37>a flaming sword</kw37> which turned every way, to guard <dn>את</dn> the way of <kw15>the tree of life</kw15>.
